passage: The Class 5 hall at the community school was decorated with balloons for the surprise for Maria, the class teacher, who had a birthday. Dilnaz stood by the door with a big card behind her back. Her heart was thumping, and she wanted to shout. But when Maria came in, Dilnaz kept her face perfectly plain and said, "Good morning, Ma'am," in the usual voice. Ma'am gave her a suspicious look. Dilnaz's friends were nearly bursting with laughter. Only when everybody yelled "Happy birthday!" did Dilnaz bring out the card, grinning wide. Maria laughed and said, "You had me fooled!"

qa.q: What was Dilnaz holding behind her back?
qa.a: She was holding a big card.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling while she kept her face plain, and why did she hold back?
qa.a: She was excited, with her heart thumping, and she kept her face plain to keep the surprise until the right moment. Her wide grin at the end shows the excitement was there all along.

qa.q: What could adults do to make the most of a child's kept-in excitement?
qa.a: Enjoy the delay and let the child reveal the surprise in the right moment, as Maria did by laughing along.

qa.q: How might Maria have felt on entering the room and seeing Dilnaz's plain face?
qa.a: Maria looked suspicious, so she may have sensed something was up and was curious. She then felt delighted and surprised.

grounding: A child keeps a straight face at a surprise while feeling excitement, waiting for the right moment, and the adult enjoys the delay.

passage: Manoj, who lives next door, told me what he saw. "Dhruv came back from school with the biggest smile I've ever seen, but only in his eyes. His face was calm, like a statue. I asked him how his day was and he said, 'Fine,' very serious. But his fingers kept tapping and he bounced on his toes. I thought something was up. Then his mother came out of the house and he burst out, 'I won the drawing prize!' and held up a golden ribbon. He'd been saving it for her. I said 'Congratulations,' and he grinned at me. I think he wanted it to be a surprise."

qa.q: What did Dhruv hold up when his mother came out?
qa.a: He held up a golden ribbon.

qa.q: What might Dhruv's calm face with tapping fingers have meant, and what else did Manoj consider?
qa.a: It probably meant excitement kept in until he could tell his mother. Manoj only thought something was up and could not be sure.

qa.q: What could Dhruv's mother do when she hears his news?
qa.a: Enjoy the surprise and share his excitement fully, since he had been holding it in for her.

qa.q: How does Manoj see Dhruv's behaviour?
qa.a: Manoj noticed his fingers tapping and bouncing but couldn't be sure of the reason, only guessing it was a surprise.

grounding: A child keeps a straight face at a surprise while feeling excitement, waiting for the right moment, as an observer guesses.

passage:
Monday: Hafsa, who helped in the school office, whispered to Omkar, "You got into the school band! But it's a secret till Friday's assembly."
Omkar's heart leapt. But he kept his face straight. "Okay," he said calmly.
Wednesday: At home, Mummy asked, "Anything new at school?" Omkar shrugged. "Nothing much." Under the table his feet were jiggling like drums.
Friday: At assembly, the principal read the names. "Omkar!" He stood up and finally let his grin burst out. He did a little jump.
Later, Mummy said, "You knew, didn't you?"
Omkar laughed. "Since Monday!"
Mummy laughed too. "You're a good secret-keeper."

qa.q: When was the band announcement?
qa.a: At Friday's assembly.

qa.q: What was Omkar feeling while keeping a straight face at home?
qa.a: Omkar felt excited and bursting to share, but held it in to keep the surprise.

qa.q: What helped Omkar keep his secret?
qa.a: He kept his face calm and let out his excitement only through his jiggling feet until the right moment.

qa.q: How might Mummy have felt when she found out Omkar knew since Monday?
qa.a: Mummy was amused and impressed that he kept the secret so well.

grounding: Over a week, a child keeps a straight face while excited, waiting for the right moment to show it.

passage:
"Ira, you want to know how to keep a secret? Let me, your Hemant Dadu, tell you.
When I was twelve, a letter came saying I'd won a scholarship. My heart nearly jumped out of my chest! But I didn't say a word at dinner. I wanted to surprise my father after the meal.
I kept my face so serious. My mother kept looking at me. She could see my toes wiggling under the table.
After dinner, I handed Papa the letter. He read it, then laughed and hugged me. My mother said, 'I knew something was up! Your toes gave you away!'
That night, the whole family laughed. The wait made the surprise even better."

qa.q: What gave Hemant away to his mother?
qa.a: His toes wiggling under the table.

qa.q: What was young Hemant feeling while keeping a serious face at dinner?
qa.a: He felt very excited and happy, but held it in to surprise his father.

qa.q: What choice inside the story made the surprise special?
qa.a: Hemant chose to wait until after dinner to share the letter, which made the moment more exciting for everyone.

qa.q: How might Hemant's mother have felt noticing his wiggling toes?
qa.a: She was curious and amused, enjoying the delay while guessing something was up.

grounding: A grandfather recalls keeping a straight face while excited, waiting for the right moment to surprise his family.

passage:
Indu found out on the rainy school bus that she'd won the class drawing prize. Her friend had seen the list.
Her heart raced. But she kept her face calm. The last time someone won, the others teased them for being a "teacher's pet."
The bus was loud, and rain battered the windows. Indu stared outside, lips pressed together, gripping her bag.
When she got home, she burst through the door. "Vaibhav! I won! I won!"
Her brother Vaibhav looked up. "Really? You didn't look happy at the bus stop."
"I was! I just didn't want anyone to tease me."
Vaibhav laughed and gave her a high five.

qa.q: What did Indu win?
qa.a: The class drawing prize.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling while staring outside the bus window?
qa.a: Indu felt excited and happy but kept a calm face to avoid being teased.

qa.q: Why did Indu keep her face calm on the bus?
qa.a: She wanted to avoid being called a teacher's pet, so she waited to share her excitement at home.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav have seen Indu at the bus stop?
qa.a: Vaibhav thought she didn't look happy, not realising she was hiding her excitement.

grounding: On a rainy bus, a child hides excitement to avoid teasing, then shares it safely at home.

passage: The list on the notice board said: KIRAN J. – DRUMS, SCHOOL BAND. Kiran read it twice, and his face stayed perfectly still. Rohit, who hadn't been picked, was standing right beside him. On the bus Kiran stared out of the window, jaw tight, fingers tapping a secret rhythm on his knee. At the door of their flat in Kolkata, his mother, Aparna, took one look at him. "Such a serious face. Bad day?" "Normal day," Kiran said flatly. Aparna raised an eyebrow, noticed the tapping fingers, then folded her arms, smiling, and waited. Kiran lasted three more seconds. Then he dropped his bag. "I GOT DRUMS!" Aparna laughed. "I knew it. Your fingers told me."

qa.q: Which instrument was Kiran picked for?
qa.a: Drums, in the school band.

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling behind his still face on the bus?
qa.a: He was thrilled and excited, as his fingers tapping a secret rhythm show, but kept a straight face, perhaps to spare Rohit or avoid teasing 🎉

qa.q: When can keeping a straight face at good news be kind?
qa.a: When someone close by, like Rohit, has just missed out, saving the celebration for later can spare their feelings.

qa.q: How did Aparna experience Kiran's serious face at the door?
qa.a: She saw through it thanks to the tapping fingers and clearly enjoyed waiting for him to burst.

grounding: It shows a child keeping a straight face while excited, waiting for the right moment, and a parent enjoying the delay.
